name: Moon (Paragon Hag Family)
body:
Although moon hags* claim divine inspiration or even divinity, their gifts seem to leave the receiver unhinged from reality. Their families are marked by their fluid forms, strange blessings, and the trail of madness left in their wake.

Family Spells: faerie fire (3rd), darkness (6th), deep slumber (9th), confusion (12th), shadow evocation (15th), beast shape IV (18th)
Ritual Spells–Knowledge (Religion): dominate person (5th), nightmare (7th), shadow walk (9th), sympathetic* greater hag’s touch* (11th), symbol of insanity (13th), sympathetic* insanity (15th), sympathetic* polymorph any object (17th), anchored* prismatic wall (19th)
Family Abilities: The families of moon hags are varied, from those with unshakable faith in their divine heritage to those too ashamed to admit their ancestry. Regardless of their opinion, they glow with the moon’s secret light.
Lunar Mantle (Su)

You can glow with a silver light as bright as a torch. Any creature that can see the light is dazzled on attacks against you (-1 to attack). The light is not visible if you are wearing armor or have any other form of concealment. You may activate or deactivate the light as a standard action. For the purposes of interaction with darkness effects, lunar mantle has a spell level of 1 at 1st level, increasing by +1 every two paragon hag levels thereafter to a maximum of 9 at 17th level.

Lunar Blast (Su)

At 4th level, you can spend a soul point while your lunar mantle is active to fire a beam of concentrated moonlight. It is resolved as a ranged touch attack, dealing 1d6 damage for every two paragon hag levels you possess.

Infected lycanthropes stuck by the beam immediately transform as though exposed to the full moon. Anyone else struck is blinded for 1d6 rounds. Either may attempt a Fortitude save with a DC equal to 10 + 1/2 your paragon hag level + your Charisma modifier to avoid these additional effects.

Lunar Grace (Ex)

At 8th level, you gain a bonus equal to your Charisma bonus (if any) on all Saving Throws.

Lunar Form (Sp)

At 12th level, you may spend a soul point to cast polymorph on yourself. If you are in direct moonlight, you can do so without spending a soul point, but the effect wears off when you leave the moonlight. At 20th level, this effect becomes greater polymorph.

Tides of the Mind (Su)

At 16th level, when you cast a spell on a confused target, they must roll any save twice and take the lower result. You may also ignore the spell’s restrictions on type (for example, to cast charm person on non-humanoids), but not the target’s immunities.

Legendary Family

Upon reaching 20th level, you are now a well-spring of divine power. Clerics and warpriests who worship you can now gain spells. Select three domains from: alignment domains matching your alignment, Animal, Charm, Darkness, Liberation, Luck, Madness, Magic, and Trickery. You also add the spells from those domains to your spells known and ritual spells at the levels they would be granted by the domain.
